name: eight-hour-block-eight-hour-spacing
rationale: The block/spacing dose-response has risen monotonically at the diagnostic capitals through 1h/1h (500,000 JPY Sharpe +1.88), 2h/2h (+3.00, 2026-09-25) and 4h/4h (+8.05, 2026-10-01), and 2026-10-01 noted the curve has not yet peaked. Ekren/Liu/Muhle-Karbe show that a fixed-frequency rebalancing rule under proportional costs has an interior optimum interval (scaling as cost^(2/3)), so the curve must eventually turn over; doubling to 8h/8h locates where. Rebalancing three times a day is close to static, so the expected outcome is a further narrowing of the static-mix deficit with very few trades, which the trade-count criterion will refuse; the value is in mapping the curve for the pending human decision on that criterion.

paper_reference.title: Optimal Rebalancing Frequencies for Multidimensional Portfolios
paper_reference.authors: Ibrahim Ekren, Ren Liu, Johannes Muhle-Karbe
paper_reference.key_claim: Under small proportional transaction costs epsilon, the asymptotically optimal fixed rebalancing interval scales as epsilon^(2/3) and is longer when costs are high or volatility is low; its welfare loss is of the same order as the optimal no-trade-region strategy.
paper_reference.pros: shirube's rebalance_interval_secs + signal_block_secs pair is exactly a fixed-frequency rebalancing rule, and its measured cost (fee + slippage ~0.2% one-way at 50,000 JPY) is large relative to edge, which is the regime where the paper predicts long intervals; it also predicts an interior optimum, which the monotone curve observed so far has not yet reached.
paper_reference.cons: Continuous-time diffusion model with a known Merton-style target and small epsilon, not a noisy TA-driven target on 1-minute BTC/JPY bars with a 0.001 BTC lot minimum and tiered fees; gives a scaling law, not a value in hours, so it motivates extending the curve rather than choosing 8h specifically.
